data.exact_reserve_text: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 10.1m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2016: GBP 2.6m) arising predominantly from the nuclear property class (2016: predominantly from the nuclear liability class).

prior_year_events.event_name: Dropped steam generator during refurbishment of a plant in France
prior_year_events.impact_description: A reserve was established in 2016 for a dropped steam generator during refurbishment of a plant in France; this reserve was not required and was released during 2017.

named_events.loss_description: Following the Fukushima accident in March 2011, an extensive review of the Syndicate's potential catastrophe exposure was undertaken.

Largest insured windstorm loss to date was from a spares warehouse on a nuclear site from Hurricane Andrew in 1992; warehouse was damaged, with losses in the region of $200m, there was no damage to the nuclear unit.
All the plants in the vicinity of the tracks of Hurricane's Harvey, Irma and Maria, in 2017 performed to plan and, as expected, there were no significant claims advices from these events.

Policies with exposures in Japan currently exclude cover for damage arising from earthquake or tsunami perils; following the Fukushima tsunami event, residual exposures were considered and some limited cover was considered where appropriate.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate opened 2017 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 45.337m. During 2017 the Syndicate recorded a release of prior year technical reserves of GBP 10.1m (approximately 22.3% of opening gross claims outstanding), driven predominantly by favourable claims development in the nuclear property class. A reserve previously established in 2016 for a dropped steam generator during refurbishment of a French plant was not required and was released in 2017. No quantified adverse prior-year deterioration is reported.
raw_causal_phrases: the Syndicate released GBP 10.1m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2016: GBP 2.6m) arising predominantly from the nuclear property class (2016: predominantly from the nuclear liability class).

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding and the explicit prior year movement are taken from the Technical Reserves note (note 16) and the Movement in prior year's provision note (note 4) respectively and are high confidence. The claims development triangle is present in the report but cell-level extraction was not performed here; a named reserve release event (dropped steam generator in France) is explicitly referenced and linked to the 2016 reserve release. Premium segmentation is taken from the regulatory segmental analysis; a consolidated 'Reinsurance acceptances' line was used per instructions.
